author.design_notes:
File: src/curricumap/taxonomies/elt_yok_2018.yaml. I deleted the old file without reading it, for blinding, then rewrote it. It keeps id elt_yok_2018, label 'ELT Teacher Education Curriculum (YÖK 2018)', locale tr/locale-aware, ordered_rules, fuzzy disabled, unmatched: flag, and the five domains in the given order. No other file was modified.

RULES (9), in evaluation order:
1. literature: edebiyat, plus \bedeb.
2. linguistics: dilbilim, edimbilim, dil edinim, dil ve toplum, dünya ingilizce, plus a word-bounded \bsöylem\b, so that 'söyleme' (singing) is not caught.
3. language_skills, four skills: okuma, yazma, dinleme, sesletim, sözlü iletişim, dil/anlatım beceri. A bare 'beceri' is avoided because life-, study- or thinking-skills courses would match.
4. language_skills, system and use: dilbilgisi (never confused with dilbilim), sözcük, İngilizcenin yapı, çeviri, kitle iletişim.
5. pedagogy, teaching and learning: öğretim, öğretmen, öğrenme, plus ÖĞR./ÖĞRT.
6. pedagogy, education as a field. 'eğitim' is accepted only as a whole word or with -e/-de/-in/-inde, never the bare possessive 'X Eğitimi'. That keeps out Beden Eğitimi ve Spor, Müzik Eğitimi and the GK course İnsan Hakları ve Demokrasi Eğitimi. The MB 'X Eğitimi' titles are reached through learner group or setting: çocuk, yetişkin, müze, değer/karakter eğitimi. 'EĞT.' is accepted only at the start of a title.
7. pedagogy, school/classroom, guidance, assessment, psychology, thinking, special needs, materials: okul, \bsınıf\b, rehber, ölçme, değerlendir, psikoloji, düşünme, hiperaktivite, kaynaştırma, materyal, ders kitabı/içeriği.
8. general_ed, common compulsory courses: atatürk/inkılap, türk dili, bilişim/bilgisayar, topluma hizmet. 'Türkçe' and 'Yabancı Dil' use lookaheads so that the Çeviri courses and 'Yabancı Dil Öğretimi' are never candidates. An R4 regex covers second foreign languages printed by name (Almanca, Fransızca, ...).
9. general_ed, GK electives: one stem per topic, plus ^bilim (anchored, because 'bilim' also occurs inside Dilbilimi and Eğitim Bilimine Giriş) and ^drama (only the stand-alone 2006 GK Drama is general_ed).

ORDER RATIONALE (also in the header): subject before method, so compound '<subject> ... Öğretimi' titles go to their subject. Disciplines (literature, linguistics) come before skill stems. General education comes last with distinctive stems only. Zero overrides were needed.

TOLERANCE: every keyword containing a Turkish-specific letter has a regex twin with [iı] [öo] [üu] [şs] [çc] [gğ] [âa]. This matters because ASCII-uppercase 'I' casefolds to 'ı', so 'INGILIZ' becomes 'ıngılız'. A mechanical check found 0 keywords without a working twin.

GENERALISATION, on variants I generated from the official titles (excluding the conflicting row):
- 157/157 correct for Turkish uppercase, ASCII uppercase, ASCII mixed case, ASCII lowercase, Roman/Arabic numeral swap, punctuation changes, 'Dil Bilimi'/'Dil Bilgisi' spacing, apostrophes and 'İng.' abbreviations.
- 50/50 on hand-written registrar truncations such as 'ATATÜRK İLK. VE İNK. TAR. I', 'İNG. DİL BEC. ÖĞR. II', 'YAB. DİL ÖĞR. MATERYAL İNC. VE GEL.' and 'TOPLUMA HİZ. UYG.'.
- No variant was ever misclassified. The only residual misses are unmatched, and only when 'Eğitim' is abbreviated to 'EĞT.' after a qualifier: 7/157 with 'EĞT.' forced everywhere, e.g. 'Özel Eğt.' or 'Türk Eğt. Tarihi'. This is a deliberate trade-off, because a non-initial 'EĞT.' cannot be told apart from 'Beden Eğt.'.
- Off-programme titles (Beden Eğitimi ve Spor, Müzik Eğitimi, Matematik, Fizik, Veri Yapıları, Şarkı Söyleme, Yaşam Becerileri, Sınıflandırma, Trafik Eğitimi, Hazırlık İngilizcesi and others) stay unmatched. Only Sanat Eğitimi, İş Sağlığı ve Güvenliği and Din Kültürü ve Ahlak Bilgisi map, to general_ed via the official GK stems sanat/sağlık/kültür.

OUT OF SCOPE BY DESIGN: English-language titles, and courses absent from both YÖK lists (e.g. Anlambilim, Roman, Şiir). These are left unmatched and flagged rather than guessed.

issues.problem: In rule 6 the eğitim regex '\be[gğ][iı]t[iı]m(e|de|[iı]n|[iı]nde)?\b' does not do what its comment says. The comment says 'X Eğitimi' compounds (training in a subject, e.g. Beden Eğitimi, Müzik Eğitimi) are never accepted. But '-inde' is the possessive-locative of exactly that compound (eğitim-i-nde), so they come back in. Test results: 'Beden Eğitiminde Oyun' -> pedagogy (ambiguous=False). 'Müzik Eğitiminde Bilgisayar' -> pedagogy. The official titles use only these forms of eğitim: bare, -e, -de and possessive -i. So '-in' and '-inde' are undeclared generalisations. That contradicts the SOURCE claim that the rules 'add only generic registrar renderings'.
issues.fix: Either (a) use '\be[gğ][iı]t[iı]m(e|de|[iı]n)?\b'. I tested this in memory: 157/0/14 unchanged, 0 variant changes, synth still passes. The trade-off is that 'Yabancı Dil Eğitiminde Teknoloji Kullanımı' becomes unmatched (flagged) instead of pedagogy-ambiguous. Or (b) keep '-inde' and rewrite the comment and the SOURCE line. They should say that the possessive-locative 'X Eğitiminde Y' is accepted on purpose as a teaching-method shape and that it lets in 'Beden/Müzik Eğitiminde ...'.

issues.problem: The rule 8 'Yabancı Dil' regex is under-constrained. It sends institution-specific ELT pedagogy electives to general_ed without any ambiguity flag. The regex is '\byab(anc[ıi]|\.) ?d[iı]l(?! [öo][gğ]r)', and its lookahead rejects only a following 'öğr'. Rule 6 deliberately rejects the possessive 'Eğitimi'. So any 'Yabancı Dil + <anything but öğr…>' title falls through to general_ed. Results: 'Yabancı Dil Eğitimi', 'YABANCI DIL EGITIMI', 'Erken Yaşta Yabancı Dil Eğitimi', 'Yabancı Dil Eğitimi Politikaları', 'Yabancı Dil Kaygısı', 'Yabancı Dil Sınıflarında Drama', 'Yabancı Dil Sınıflarında Teknoloji Kullanımı', 'Yabancı Dil Olarak İngilizce' and 'Yabancı Dil Sınavlarına Hazırlık' all go to general_ed (ambiguous=False, span 'yabancı dil'). One CALL course also gets two domains: 'Bilgisayar Destekli Dil Öğretimi' goes to pedagogy, but 'Bilgisayar Destekli Dil Eğitimi' and 'Bilgisayar Destekli Yabancı Dil Eğitimi' go to general_ed via 'bilgisayar' (ambiguous=False). The rule 8 comment says foreign-language teaching courses 'are never candidates here', which overstates the guard. In the ablation, only the five titles 'Yabancı Dil 1/2' and 'İkinci Yabancı Dil I/II/III' need this regex.
issues.fix: Whitelist the official shape instead of blacklisting one continuation: '^(\S+ )?yab(anc[ıi]|\.) ?d[iı]l(\s+([ıiv]+|\d+)\b|\s*[(:]|$)'. This covers Yabancı Dil 1, İkinci Yabancı Dil III, Mesleki Yabancı Dil, 'Yabancı Dil (Almanca) I' and 'Seçmeli Yabancı Dil: Almanca'. Add '\bd[iı]l e[gğ][iı]t[iı]m' to rule 6, because language education is pedagogy. In rule 7, allow inflected forms of sınıf with '\bs[ıi]n[ıi]f(?!land)', which still excludes sınıflandırma. Tested in memory: Eğitimi/Politikaları/Sınıflarında and both Bilgisayar Destekli ... Eğitimi titles go to pedagogy; Kaygısı and Olarak İngilizce become unmatched. The R4 language-name regex sits in rule 8, after rules 1-4. As a result, 'Almanca Dilbilgisi I', 'ALMANCA DILBILGISI I', 'Fransızca Okuma-Yazma', 'Almanca Yazma Becerileri', 'İspanyolca Sözlü İletişim', 'Fransızca Dinleme ve Sesletim', 'Almanca Sözcük Bilgisi' and 'Almanca-Türkçe Çeviri' all go to language_skills. 'Türkçe Okuma ve Yazma' and 'Türkçe Dilbilgisi' go to language_skills (ambiguous), and 'Türk Dilbilgisi' goes to language_skills unflagged. The plain forms are handled correctly: 'Almanca I' and 'İkinci Yabancı Dil (Almanca) I' go to general_ed. 'Korece I', 'Farsça I' and 'Latince' are unmatched, which is acceptable because they are surfaced.

Give it the plain keywords any: ['atatürk', 'inkılap', 'almanca'] so the synthetic names 'atatürk 1', 'inkılap 2', 'almanca 3' still classify (verified). Give it these regexes: '^t[üu]rk d[iı]l[iı]\b(?!.*[öo][gğ]r)'; '^(akadem[iı]k )?t[üu]rk[çc]e\b(?!.*([çc]ev[iı]r|[öo][gğ]r))'; the whitelisted Yabancı Dil regex from the first issue; the language-name regex extended with korece, farsça, yunanca and latince; and '\b(alman|frans[ıi]z|rus|[iı]spanyol|[iı]talyan|arap|japon|[çc][iı]n|t[üu]rk|d[iı]van|halk) edeb'. The synthetic pedagogy names become 'öğretim 1', 'öğretmen 2', 'öğretim 3', which still classify correctly with no ambiguity (verified).

So the very course that the header and the rule 6 comment cite as excluded goes to pedagogy with ambiguous=False: 'Beden Eğitim ve Spor I', 'BEDEN EĞİTİM VE SPOR' and 'BEDEN EGITIM VE SPOR I'. It also decides assessment-of-skill titles, against the official convention that assessment courses are pedagogy. Yet 'Ölçme ve Değerlendirme', 'Yabancı Dil Öğretiminde Ölçme ve Değerlendirme', 'İngilizce Öğretiminde Sınav Hazırlama ve Değerlendirme' and 'Sınıf İçi Öğrenmelerin Değerlendirilmesi' are all pedagogy. The second option must be checked against 'İngilizce Dil Becerilerinin Öğretimi', which has to stay language_skills.

hazards.verdict:
The taxonomy is not safe against false positives yet, and should be revised before it is used on registrar data. The fixes are cheap and I verified them in memory.

**What checks out.** The header's claims are accurate:
- 157/158 official titles are correct. The only miss is 2006 'Türk Eğitim Tarihi'. It is an unavoidable label conflict: the 2018 programme has the identical title as MB.
- 0 titles are unmatched and 14 are flagged ambiguous.
- The counts are right: 9 rules, 61 keywords, 36 regexes, 0 overrides.
- Registrar renderings of the official titles cause no new wrong assignments. I tried Turkish uppercase, ASCII upper and lower case, and Roman/Arabic numeral swaps. Mid-title abbreviations such as 'EĞT.' only produce unmatched titles.
- The synthetic catalogue (seed 7; 446 rows for 30 students, 878 for 60) classifies correctly with no ambiguity.

**What fails.** I ran about 280 plausible off-programme titles through assign_domain. More than 50 got a wrong domain with ambiguous=False, and more than 25 more were wrong but flagged.

Most of the courses named in the brief behave well:
- 'Beden Eğitimi ve Spor', 'Müzik' and 'Afet Bilinci' are unmatched.
- 'Girişimcilik', 'Almanca I' and 'Bilgisayar Programlama' go to general_ed.

'Türk Dili ve Edebiyatı' goes to literature; it is flagged, but the assignment is wrong.

There are three root causes:
1. **Bare stems.** okuma, yazma, dinleme, kitle iletişim, öğrenme, değerlendir, psikoloji, rehber and müze are unconstrained substrings, and '\bedeb' also matches 'edebilme'.
2. **Rule order.** The R2/R4 general_ed rules run last, so these go to English domains:
   - second-language courses with a skill word, e.g. 'Almanca Dilbilgisi I';
   - Turkish-language courses with a skill word;
   - non-English literature, e.g. 'Alman Edebiyatı', which goes to literature unflagged.
   
   Meanwhile the unanchored 'Yabancı Dil' regex pulls ELT pedagogy electives into general_ed: 'Yabancı Dil Eğitimi', 'Yabancı Dil Kaygısı' and 'Yabancı Dil Sınıflarında Drama'.
3. **Anchors weaker than their comments claim.** '^drama\b' is not limited to the stand-alone title, and whole-word 'eğitim' admits 'Beden Eğitim ve Spor'.

**Candidate fix, tested in memory only (no file written).** The patch adds one new general_ed rule at the top for R2/R4 languages and constrains the stems as described in the issues. With it:
- Every unflagged misassignment that the issues propose a fix for is gone.
- The official titles are unchanged: 157/158 correct, 0 unmatched, 14 ambiguous.
- The registrar-variant results are identical.
- The synthetic catalogue still classifies correctly with no ambiguity.

The synthetic course names change to sesletim/sözlü iletişim/dil beceri, öğretim 3 and almanca 3. The paper's alpha values cannot change, because grades are aggregated by course_id and course_name only feeds classification and the unmapped list.

**Protocol.** I read only src/, tests/ and validation/data/yok_programmes.csv, and edited no files. I did not run pytest, because it writes cache and temp files. Instead I reproduced test_every_bundled_taxonomy_classifies_its_synthetic_courses and the paper example's 878-row, zero-ambiguity checks in memory. I have not verified test_bundled_sample_transcript_runs_as_documented: its toy file is outside my allowed read scope.

generality.verdict:
The rules handle character-level variants well but are fragile at the word level. Two abbreviation gaps send official titles to the wrong domain without any flag, so issues 1 and 2 should be fixed before calling the file generalised.

Checked with curricumap.classify.assign_domain on src/curricumap/taxonomies/elt_yok_2018.yaml.

**What the author claims, and holds:**
- 157/158 source titles correct, 0 unmatched, 14 ambiguous.
- 9 rules, 61 keywords, 36 regexes, 0 overrides.
- The one miss is the 2006 GK "Türk Eğitim Tarihi". It cannot be fixed: the identical title is pedagogy in 2018 and general_ed in 2006.
- The goal-5 synthetic courses all classify correctly, with 0 ambiguous. I checked this in memory rather than with pytest, because pytest's temp folders sit under the /tmp area the blinding rules put off limits.

**Rendering variants: 0 failures** across all 157 non-conflicting titles for:
- Turkish uppercase, and uppercase from a non-Turkish locale (e.g. "DILBILIMI").
- Full ASCII folding in upper, title and lower case.
- Roman/Arabic numeral swaps, hyphenated numerals, and colons/hyphens removed.
- Fixed-width truncation at 35 characters or more.
- The [iı]/[öo]/[çc]/[gğ] handling is thorough, and the rules mostly capture course families through stems.

**Where it breaks: abbreviations are supported unevenly.**
- The teaching stem accepts "ÖĞR."/"ÖĞRT." anywhere in a title.
- Several subject stems, which are supposed to win under the subject-before-method order, do not accept their common abbreviations: "EDB.", "ÇEV.", "SOSYODİLB.", "EDİMB.", "SÖZC.".
- So compound "subject + Öğretimi" titles and the two 2006 translation courses land in pedagogy or general_ed with ambiguous=False.
- In 43 targeted registrar probes, the current file leaves 30 unmatched and puts 13 in the wrong domain.
- In a sweep that abbreviates one word at a time in every official title (1,321 variants, most of them unrealistic), there are 39 wrong-domain results. Every one comes from those two mechanisms, plus one unrealistic case (shortening "Dünya" in "Dünya İngilizceleri ve Kültür").
- Title-start anchors (^bilim, ^drama, ^eğt.) and phrase patterns that need every word in full leave more official variants unmatched.

**Proposed fix set (all regexes are in the issues below; tested in memory only, the YAML was not edited):**
- Source titles stay at 157/158 with 0 unmatched.
- 43/43 probes pass.
- Rendering variants stay at 0 failures, and the 2 wrong results in the 20–40 character truncation sweep go to 0.
- Wrong-domain results in the sweep drop from 39 to 13, with the optional frame guard in issue 1. The 13 left need unrealistic abbreviations such as "BCR." or "SZC.".
- Ambiguity flags drop from 14 to 7.
- Precision is unchanged: "Beden Eğitimi ve Spor", "BEDEN EĞT. VE SPOR", "Müzik Eğitimi", "ÇEVRE EĞT.", "Sözleşme Hukuku", "Sosyoloji" and "Pragmatizm" stay unmatched.
- The 25 key regexes parse unchanged from single-quoted YAML.

Not checked: the full pytest suite, and examples/sample_transcript.csv, which is outside the files I was allowed to read.

issues.problem: Compound '<subject> ... Öğretimi' titles go to pedagogy with no flag when the subject word is abbreviated. Rule order puts subjects before teaching, but that only works if the subject stem matches. Rule 5 accepts 'ÖĞR.'/'ÖĞRT.' anywhere via '\b[öo][gğ]r(t|et)?\.'. The literature stems ('edebiyat', '\bedeb') do not accept 'EDB.', TDK's standard abbreviation for edebiyat. The linguistics and vocabulary stems need near-full words ('dilbilim', 'ed[iı]m ?b[iı]l[iı]m', 's[öo]zc[üu]k'). Only one domain matches, so the ambiguity flag (the header's safety net for compound titles) does not fire. Results: 'DİL VE EDB. ÖĞR. I' -> pedagogy via '\b[öo][gğ]r(t|et)?\.' (amb=False); 'DİL VE EDB. ÖĞRETİMİ 2' -> pedagogy via 'öğretim' (amb=False); 'EDB. VE DİL ÖĞR. I' -> pedagogy; 'SOSYODİLB. VE DİL ÖĞR.' -> pedagogy; 'EDİMB. VE DİL ÖĞR.' -> pedagogy; 'EDİM BİL. VE DİL ÖĞR.' -> pedagogy; 'İNG. SÖZC. BİLGİSİ ÖĞR.' -> pedagogy, all with amb=False. 'İNG. EDB. I' and 'İNGİLİZ EDB. II' -> unmatched. Rule 4: replace 's[öo]zc[üu]k' with '\bs[öo]zc'. Optional structural guard (also tested): stop the generic teaching stems from matching the 'X ve Dil Öğretimi' / 'Dil ve X Öğretimi' frame. All 7 official titles in that frame are subject courses, so an unrecognised subject is then flagged unmatched instead of labelled pedagogy. Rule 5 becomes any: ["öğretmen", "öğrenme"], which still satisfies goal 5 (synthetic test passes), with regex: ['^(?!.*\b(ve d[iı]l|d[iı]l ve \S+) [öo][gğ]r).*\b[öo][gğ]re[tn]', '^(?!.*\b(ve d[iı]l|d[iı]l ve \S+) [öo][gğ]r).*\b[öo][gğ]r[^\s.]{0,4}\.']. issues.problem: The two 2006 translation courses go to general_ed with no flag whenever 'Çeviri' is not written out in full. Rule 4 only knows the full stem ('çeviri', '[çc]ev[iı]r[iı]'). Rule 8's Türkçe regex excludes translation with a lookahead keyed to that same stem: '\bt[üu]rk[çc]e\b(?!.*[çc]ev[iı]r)'. 'ÇEV.' is the standard Turkish abbreviation of çeviri/çeviren. Results: 'İNGİLİZCE-TÜRKÇE ÇEV.' -> general_ed via the Türkçe regex (amb=False); 'TÜRKÇE-İNGİLİZCE ÇEV.' -> general_ed. The 20-character truncations 'İNGİLİZCE-TÜRKÇE ÇEV' and 'TÜRKÇE-İNGİLİZCE ÇEV' -> general_ed; these are the only wrong-domain results in a 20–40 character truncation sweep. With the synonym 'Tercüme', 'İNGİLİZCE-TÜRKÇE TERCÜME' and 'TÜRKÇE-İNGİLİZCE TERCÜME' -> general_ed.

Rule 4: add '[iı]ng(\.|[iı]l[iı]zce)\W*t[üu]rk[çc]e|t[üu]rk[çc]e\W*[iı]ng(\.|[iı]l[iı]zce)', optionally with '|terc[üu]me'. Rule 8: widen the lookahead to '\bt[üu]rk[çc]e\b(?!.*([çc]ev|terc[üu]m))', so an unrecognised translation title is at worst flagged. Tested: all five variants -> language_skills; 'Türkçe I: Yazılı Anlatım' and 'Türkçe II: Sözlü Anlatım' stay general_ed; the 2 wrong results in the truncation sweep go to 0.

issues.problem: 'EĞT.' is accepted only at the start of a title ('^e[gğ][iı]?t\.'), and the 'eğitim' regex needs the full word. So official MB titles whose deciding word is a trailing 'Eğitim' are lost when it is abbreviated. Results, all unmatched: 'TÜRK EĞT. TARİHİ' (2018 compulsory), 'KARŞILAŞTIRMALI EĞT.', 'KAPSAYICI EĞT.', 'ÖZEL EĞT.', 'SÜRDÜRÜLEBİLİR KALKINMA VE EĞT.', and 'KARAKTER VE DEĞER EĞT.' (both the 'değer eğitim' keyword and the '(karakter|de[gğ]er(ler)?) e[gğ][iı]t[iı]m' regex need the full word). The start anchor also fails behind any prefix: 'MB SEÇ.: EĞT. FELSEFESİ' and 'ZORUNLU - EĞT. SOSYOLOJİSİ' -> unmatched. Limiting 'EĞT.' to the start is a sound guard against the possessive in 'BEDEN EĞT.', but it drops abbreviated forms of six official titles.
issues.fix: Accept 'EĞT.' mid-title only after the modifiers that occur in the official MB 'X Eğitim' titles. Add to rule 6: '\b(özel|kapsay[ıi]c[ıi]|kar[şs][ıi]la[şs]t[ıi]rmal[ıi]|t[üu]rk|kalk[ıi]nma ve|de[gğ]er(ler)?) e[gğ][iı]?t\.'. Tested: all six -> pedagogy, while 'BEDEN EĞT. VE SPOR', 'ÇEVRE EĞT.' and 'Müzik Eğitimi' stay unmatched. Comment that this lists official modifiers on purpose, because a bare mid-title 'eğt.' would also catch 'Beden Eğt.'.

issues.problem:
Overall answer to the lens question: the rules mostly capture course families through stems, with a few full-title phrases; most single-course patterns are unavoidable. The pattern inventory in numbers:
- 58 of the 97 patterns match exactly one of the 116 distinct base courses (numerals stripped).
- Six patterns are complete official titles rather than stems: 'dil ve toplum', 'türk dili', 'etkili iletişim', 'mesleki ingilizce', 'bilgisayar', '^drama\b'. 'ingilizcenin yapı' and 'topluma hizmet' are nearly full titles.

- The header's '61 keywords, 36 regexes' overstates the vocabulary. For 52 of the 61 keywords, a regex in the same rule matches every source title the keyword matches, usually the same stem rewritten with [iı]/[öo] classes.

- The three patterns that never fire on a source title ('\b[öo][gğ]r(t|et)?\.', '^e[gğ][iı]?t\.', and the language-name list) all handle teaching or general wording, none a subject. That fits the uneven abbreviation support in issue 1.
